props.title: Six places a sound bath fits during the day.
props.lede: The session is the same in each of them. What changes is who is lying on the floor and what the venue needs to supply.

rows.text: A studio adds it as a class or a workshop on its own schedule: a Sunday morning, a Saturday afternoon, the session before a retreat weekend. The studio’s students lie down, the facilitator tunes the sound system to the studio, and for seventy-five minutes the space sounds like a different one.

A session in a conference space or on a cleared floor, inside a long lunch, for a wellness week or the week after a hard quarter. The lights go low, and the session has a stretch of real silence in the middle of it.

rows.term: A senior center or a senior living community
rows.text: A sound bath for seniors is the same session with the lights low and the floor covered in mats and blankets, and a resident who can’t get down to a mat rests in a seat or a recliner instead. Nobody is asked to do anything but rest, and the facilitator tunes the sound system to the space.

rows.term: A hospice or a recovery center
rows.text: A session for the people in care, for their families, or for the staff. The session is guided in the lightest way, nobody is asked to speak or to share, and someone who can’t lie on a mat rests where they are.
A staff day, a session for teachers at the end of a term, or a session built into a student program. A gym or a hall holds a whole staff on mats.

The morning that opens a retreat, at a lodge in the mountains or a house on the Front Range. A sound bath in the morning and live music that night is one booking on one contract, and the corporate retreats page covers the evenings.

props.html: The lights go down, everyone lies down, and the facilitator opens the session with a short ceremony. For seventy-five minutes there are live instruments played over music composed for the session, with bass deep enough to feel in your chest, and a stretch of real silence in the middle. It closes the way it opened. There’s nothing to follow and nothing to get right, and someone who sleeps through the second half has used the hour well.
Send the headcount and the space and we’ll tell you whether it fits, or hold the session in a partner space in Denver instead.

props.title: Asked about booking a daytime sound bath.

items.q: What does a venue need to host a sound bath?
items.a: Enough floor for everyone to lie down with a little space between the mats, a standard outlet, low light, and about ninety minutes before doors for the facilitator to set up and tune the sound system to the space. The sound system, the mats, the blankets and the waivers arrive with the facilitator. If your space won't work, the session runs in a partner space in Denver. Firstwater is booked through Signet Artists.

items.q: Can someone who can't lie on a mat take part?
items.a: Yes. They rest in a seat or a recliner instead, which is how a session at a senior center, a senior living community or a hospice usually runs.
Comfortable clothes, and nothing else. Phones stay in bags for the length of the session, and the longer answers, from what to wear to what it's like to be in one, are on Firstwater's own FAQ.
